From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>

Subject: CardStream MAP: evaluation commitments & security gate checkpoints

Hi Sandra —

Great talking earlier. As promised, I'm sending a concise mutual action plan (MAP) so procurement and your security team can see the remaining gates and ownership to get to a pilot purchase. High level: we plan a four-week evaluation with a small production-like workload, and acceptance depends on three security gates (SOC 2 evidence, SIG/CAIQ questionnaire, signed DPA with data retention clauses).

Key asks from CardStream (what we need from your side):
- Confirm SIG owner and point-of-contact for questionnaire (you mentioned someone on security).
- Confirm required data retention window (30/90/365 days) and regional residency constraints.
- Procurement to review the DPA redline; we can propose a narrow set of carve-outs for escrow/forensics.

What Redwood will deliver (this sprint):
- SOC 2 summary + snapshot (attached PDF).
- Pre-populated SIG spreadsheet for your team to validate (attached XLSX).
- Draft DPA redline for your legal (we'll attach v2 in the next email).

Proposed timeline (please confirm):
Week 0 (this week): SIG sent & DPA redline shared; cardstream to return SIG answers within 5 business days.
Week 2: evidence review and short call to clarify open items.
Week 3–4: run evaluation workload; acceptance test tied to successful sandbox traffic + resolved security items.

If that looks reasonable I'll loop in Kimberly from Legal to track the DPA, and Ben (CS) will set up the sandbox and acceptance tests.

Best,
Ava Chen
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Kimberly —

Forwarding the MAP note I just got from Ava. CardStream is asking for a DPA redline and we should confirm whether the procurement team will accept our standard 365-day retention default or if they require a shorter window. Also they may ask about an escrow/forensics carve-out for EU residency. Can you advise on the latest carrier-friendly language we can offer (and any must-haves legal needs)?

Quick notes for context:
- SOC 2: we have a recent Type II (Q4 2024) with scoped exclusions for partner-managed infra; summary attached.
- SIG: I've pre-filled the spreadsheet with our answers, but tech/security will need to verify a couple of PCI adjacency items.
- DPA: expect procurement redlines on subprocessor list and data deletion timing.

If you want, we can propose a mutual 30-day evidence-response SLA in the MAP to keep momentum.

—Ben

Hi Ava —

Thanks for the clear MAP. A couple of clarifications from our side before we lock dates:
1) SIG owner: that's me for now — I'll coordinate with our InfoSec analyst (J. Patel) to complete the spreadsheet. Expect answers in ~4 business days.
2) Data retention: CardStream requires 90-day customer data retention for sandbox logs, and production logs must be retained for 365 days. We also prefer US-only residency for logs containing user PII.
3) DPA: Procurement flagged two asks — (a) limit subprocessor disclosures to a redacted list until contract signature, (b) a clause for reasonable-forensics access if we suspect a breach.

We can target sandbox kickoff the week of Apr 7 if Redwood can provide the signed DPA by Apr 3 (procurement wants legal to have the signed doc before data flows). Can you confirm you can meet that date? If not, propose alternatives.

Also please send the editable DPA redline; we'll upload to our DocuSign queue once we agree.

Best,
Sandra Lopez
Sr. Security Program Manager | CardStream
s.lopez@cardstream.com

Hi Sandra —

Thanks — that timeline is helpful and reasonable. We can aim to have an agreed DPA (signed) by Apr 3 if CardStream returns any redlines by EOD Wed Mar 26. Kimberly, can legal commit to a final review turnaround of 48 business hours for redlines submitted by then?

Next steps I'll action now:
- Kimberly: adding you to this thread to own DPA redline cadence and finalize language around forensics access and limited subprocessor disclosure.
- Ben: I'll set up the sandbox environment and a short acceptance test plan (I included a draft below).
- Sandra: we will scope sandbox logs to US-only by default and provide a configuration guide for retention windows (90 days sandbox / 365 production).

Draft acceptance test (for week-of Apr 7 pilot):
- Run 5k synthetic transactions over 48 hours.
- Measure end-to-end latency P50/P95 and token-cost delta vs baseline.
- Verify logs are routed to US-only storage and retention configured to 90 days.
- SIG answers completed and SOC 2 snapshot validated.

Attachments: DPA_redline_v2.docx (DOCX)

Ava
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sandra Lopez <s.lopez@cardstream.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CardStream MAP: evaluation commitments & security gate checkpoints

All —

I reviewed the DPA redline and the forensics language. Short answers:
- We can accept a limited subprocessor disclosure approach pre-signature (redacted vendor names with full list to be shared post-signature). Add a 30-day window to provide the full list after countersignature.
- Forensics access: we are open to a narrowly scoped clause that allows CardStream to request targeted forensics data in the event of a suspected breach, subject to an approved legal request and mutual non-disclosure protections. We will not permit unfettered access to Cedar logs or internal debug dumps.
- Retention: we'll support sandbox=90 days / production=365 days; we will include an explicit configuration section in the SOW.

Timeline commitment: if CardStream returns redlines by COB Wed Mar 26, Redwood legal can complete final review and produce a countersigned DPA by Apr 2 — this gives procurement one business day to route for signature ahead of your Apr 3 target. Let's keep pressure on the Wed deadline to avoid slipping the sandbox kickoff.

I'll attach the small DPA snippet I recommend (I'll paste below) and will follow up in DocuSign when we have the redline.

—Kimberly
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

> Proposed forensics clause (draft):
> "Upon a reasonable, documented request from Customer and subject to Redwood's security and privacy safeguards and any applicable legal process, Redwood will provide targeted forensic artifacts necessary to investigate the suspected incident. Redwood will not disclose raw debug dumps or internal platform telemetry without a court order or equivalent legal process."
